cells.tense: Fairness is moving through the exchanges here without being managed, and the room is steady.
cells.act: mark the end of it with a plain act
cells.ask: Take one finished thing within reach — minor, and nobody is asking you to fix it — and close it deliberately: a word or a mark on paper, once, then leave it done.
cells.core:
There's a natural sense of proportion in how you give and take right now. You can tell when something has tipped without running numbers, and when you correct it the correction is quiet. Others leave an exchange with you feeling they got their due. That ease is doing real work, since it's what lets things finish and clear instead of dragging on.

What comes next is an ending. Not a big reckoning — one finished thing, closed deliberately so the space it takes can clear. The ease you carry is what makes a clean ending possible, so put it on something close and finish the job. After that, something else gets to start, and it'll have room.
cells.sheetLine: The fairness is easy right now, so let one finished thing stay finished.
cells.verb: putting things back to their true proportion

cells.tense: The tally will be running in the head before anything around it has actually happened.
cells.act: keep it at its real size when you are asked to shrink it
cells.ask: When something gets treated as smaller or lighter than it plainly is, name its true scale exactly once and then drop it — no follow-up, no case to win.
cells.core:
There's a ledger overhead, running ahead of events. Who gave more, who owes, how to phrase the next ask so it comes out even — the accounting starts before anyone has done anything, and it's borrowing the fairness that's supposed to be resting. It has a way of making the exchanges near you feel measured. The strength underneath is real: you can bear a lot without folding. Bearing it that way is what makes it heavier.

So for now, just keep things at their true scale. When something gets treated as smaller than it clearly is, name the scale once, plainly, and then be silent. No case, no tally, just the size of it. Test: if the size gets argued or met with silence, is the act still whole? It is — you said it, and it stayed. That's the whole task for this stretch.

cells.tense: Something was wanted and never asked for, and the person is not yet making room to ask.
cells.act: do the small practice again, alone, today
cells.ask: Once today and once tomorrow, name one plain thing you want — aloud if alone, on paper if not — and leave the outcome open without settling early.
cells.core:
Here, fair exchange runs mostly one way. There's giving and little asking, and it has a settled feel to it, like the arrangement is just how things are. What's under that calm is holding — a hand kept off the scale. The wish to ask is not covered by anything right now, and it walks past a room that's gone quiet. The person knows what fair treatment looks like, and they've stopped bringing it up.

Start small and alone, which makes it easier. Once today and once tomorrow, say one want, naming the plain thing and asking for the plain thing, with nothing added. No story, no reasons, no hedging. If it feels too large, make it smaller and do the smaller one. Then leave the answer room to arrive.

cells.tense: The tally is on, and the person whose hand is on it would not call it that.
cells.act: notice what you already know before you reason about it
cells.ask: When an old unfairness surfaces, name the plain fact of what happened before you build any case around it — the first thing you noticed, no evidence yet.
cells.core:
A quiet running tally is going in the background, and the person carrying it uses a different word for what's happening. Old unfairnesses get counted. Scores get kept. Then the next move appears, and the counting has been going on the whole time without being owned.

What this could answer with is noticing — knowing what happened before any argument is built. Not deciding who's right. Just the plain fact of it. Say it once and sit with it, and let proportion come back while the case is not being constructed. That's what takes the weight off: the tally ends when it's simply seen, not when it's won.
